The most effective methods of laundering money derived from drug sales involve complicated and multi-layered transactions designed to disguise the source of the funds. Generally, these transactions begin with physical goods such as real estate or cars that have been purchased with money generated from drug sales. The goods are then sent to companies in different locations, which act as “shell” companies because their purpose is simply to mask the money’s true origin. These companies then sell the goods and deposit the profit into bank accounts established for that purpose. Once settled in these accounts, wire transfers can be sent back to make purchases which appear legitimate on paper but were actually derived from illicit activity. Similarly, shell corporations can also be used to open bank accounts at financial institutions around the world which further serve this purpose by making it hard for law enforcement agencies to trace funds back to their original source.(https://www.inquisitr.com/5751834/how-to-launder-money-from-drug-dealing/)

The scheme involves converting illegally obtained funds into seemingly legitimate financial assets, all without raising suspicion from regulatory agencies.

According to our sources, one such method involves transferring funds to foreign countries and then bringing them back into the U.S. as legally acquired assets. This practice, known as 'round-tripping,' has been used by criminal organizations to bypass scrutiny and maintain their ill-gotten gains.
